task_context.problem_statement: Find the sum of the coefficients in the polynomial $-2(x^7 - x^4 + 3x^2 - 5) + 4(x^3 + 2x) - 3(x^5 - 4)$.
task_context.reference_solution: The sum of the coefficients in the polynomial $-2(x^7 - x^4 + 3x^2 - 5) + 4(x^3 + 2x) - 3(x^5 - 4)$ is $-2 (1 - 1 + 3 - 5) + 4 (1 + 2) - 3 (1 - 4) = (-2) \cdot (-2) + 4 \cdot 3 - 3 \cdot (-3) = \boxed{25}$.  (The sum of the coefficients in a polynomial can be found by setting the variable equal to 1.)

messages.content: I'm stuck on this math problem: Find the sum of the coefficients in the polynomial $-2(x^7 - x^4 + 3x^2 - 5) + 4(x^3 + 2x) - 3(x^5 - 4)$. Do I have to expand the whole thing first?

You certainly could expand everything and combine like terms, but that would take a lot of time and leave more room for small errors. There is a much faster shortcut for finding the sum of coefficients of any polynomial. Think about what happens to the terms of a polynomial if you replace the variable $x$ with a specific number.
If I put in 0, I just get the constant term. But I need the sum of all of them. What if I put in 1?

Exactly! When you substitute $x = 1$, every power of $x$ becomes 1, which effectively leaves you with just the coefficients. So, instead of expanding the expression, you can just evaluate the entire polynomial at $x = 1$. Why don't you try plugging 1 into the expression and see what you get?
Your calculations for each section are spot on, and your final summation is correct. The sum of the coefficients is indeed 25. Great job applying the shortcut!
